format: Masked contract sheet (Stage E.32b). Keys of 'contracts' are random contract labels (K-xxxx); the same label names the same contract everywhere in both sheets. Each contract has seven evidence lists: D2a_automated_share (automated or HFT share of volume for the product, its group or a related market), D2b_programs (market-maker, lead market-maker and volume-incentive programs), D3_s1_relationships (spread, cointegration, lead-lag relationships with horizon), D3_s2_scheduled_releases (scheduled releases, timing, absorption speed), D3_s3_session_structure (session handoffs, pauses, settlement windows), Sat_iii_price_discovery (information-share or price-discovery studies) and D6_directional_evidence (intraday directional studies). Every item has a fresh id (I-xxxxxx), 'applies_to' (one of: this contract; a same-underlying sibling; the product group; a close cousin (same asset class on CME Globex); the asset class broadly or a multi-asset study; another venue of the same underlying), the reader's value, window (data period or dates in force), detail and verbatim quote with product codes, product names, firm and platform names replaced by labels or '[other product]', references replaced by '[ref]', and 'verified': full text; abstract [unverified]; snippet [unverified]; or reused from an earlier stage (level as its text states). D6 items also carry keyword flags after_2010, out_of_sample, net_of_costs and horizon, derived mechanically from the reader's text (the text is authoritative; null = not stated). pointer_only = the reader marked it a pointer, never a source alone; negative_finding = a null or negative result. 'extended-hours' replaces the abbreviation for electronic or extended trading hours. Asset-class words (for example 'crude oil', 'weekly inventory report') are kept. The sheet carries no ADV, contract size, multiplier, tick, fee, settlement method, sibling or leader facts.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: EIA WPSR price effect: absorbed within the [-5,+10] minute window; 5-min and 30-min windows give very close estimates
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Alquist, Ellwanger and Jin (2020), Bank of Canada SWP 2020-8. Absorption: the authors chose the +10-min window as sufficient for incorporation, and report estimates for 5-min and 30-min windows 'very close' to the 15-min benchmark (robustness tables for asset responses instrumented by oil returns). Reading: absorbed within about 5-10 minutes; no documented continuation to 30 minutes in this study.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: this interval allows for sufficient time for the news to be incorporated in oil futures and other asset prices | the point estimates for the shorter and longer window sizes are very close to the benchmark results.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: API and EIA crude-inventory surprises both move 15-minute K-LRVK returns; EIA effect about twice API's
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Ye and Karali (2015), AAEA poster (precursor of Energy Economics 2016). 15-minute windows 10:25-10:40 ET (EIA) and 16:25-16:40 ET (API). Coefficients on crude shock: API -0.134/-0.126, EIA -0.231/-0.247. Absorption beyond 15 minutes not tested. 11 of 50 EIA reports produced significant return jumps; only 1 jump in the API window.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: The impact of crude oil inventory surprises in EIA report is almost twice the impact of the surprise in API reports. | In total, 11 out of 50 EIA reports generated significant return jumps.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: EIA response is immediate, effects last about 25 minutes, then the price reverts quickly
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: WTI futures around EIA reports (period not in abstract)
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Geman and Li, Journal of Energy Markets (E.20 gives 11(2), 2018; volume and year not shown on the IDEAS page), 'An analysis of intraday market response to crude oil inventory shocks'. Abstract only. Volatility and volume elevated about 25 minutes; price effect reverts quickly (reversal, not drift). Also a pre-release move 10:20-10:25 strategy (see T6 item 31).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: Market activity, in terms of price return, volatility and trading volume, responds to inventory shock very quickly, with the effects lasting for about twenty-five minutes. Our results suggest that a positive (negative) inventory shock will result in an immediate price decline (rise), while both kinds of shock increase volatility and trading volume; however, the price reverts quickly after the initial reaction.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: US macro releases (nonfarm payrolls, retail sales, others at 8:30 and 10:00 ET) cause oil-futures jumps; response 'very rapid'
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Elder, Miao and Ramchander (2013), Energy Journal 34(3):217-237 (CSU repository). More than 30% of nonfarm-payroll releases followed by jumps (23 of 72). Jump detection at 5-minute sampling. Speed: rapid (within the 5-minute sampling interval); no post-release drift reported.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: employment situation report plays a key role, with more than 30% of the announcements on the change in nonfarm payrolls followed by jumps in oil prices. | oil prices respond very rapidly to new economic data

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: EIA crude-inventory shock does not predict nearby K-LRVK returns after the release (10:35-11:00 and 11:00-15:00 ET); it does predict returns in the 30 minutes and overnight before (leakage)
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Luo and Kang (Illinois Institute of Technology), 'A Closer Look at High-frequency Prices and Trading Activities', ACFR conference paper (working paper). Absorption: within the 10:30-10:35 interval; no drift from 10:35 to 15:00 ET. Pre-release predictability is conditional on the ex-post shock (not an ex-ante signal). Text from a Firecrawl directQuote extraction of the PDF (raw PDF blocked by Cloudflare).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: we find that the inventory shock has no power to explain the return in the subsequent period after announcement (10:35AM to 11:00AM Wednesday) as well as in the remaining period (11:00AM to 3:00PM Wednesday)

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: after positive EIA surprises K-LRVK over-reacts: average drop about 0.5%, half reversed four hours later
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Rousse and Sevi (2016), FEEM NDL2016-070 (Energy Journal 2019). Post-release movement over hours is a partial reversal, not a continuation (drift) of the initial move.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: days with positive surprises are characterized by a large average price drop of about 0.5% – traders take short positions as inventories are larger than expected – which is partly corrected in the hours following the news release. Four hours later, the drop is half as large, i.e. 0.25%.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: announcement-day effect and pre-release anticipation at daily frequency (futures and options)
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Miao, Ramchander, Wang and Yang (2017 version), 'The Impact of Crude Oil Inventory Announcements on Prices: Evidence from Derivatives Markets' (CSU repository). Daily horizon only; no intraday absorption measure.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: We document evidence of a strong announcement day effect on both markets, and find prices to move in anticipation of the inventory surprise.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: API and EIA crude-inventory surprises both move 15-minute K-LRVK returns; EIA effect about twice API's
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Ye and Karali (2015), AAEA poster (precursor of Energy Economics 2016). 15-minute windows 10:25-10:40 ET (EIA) and 16:25-16:40 ET (API). Coefficients on crude shock: API -0.134/-0.126, EIA -0.231/-0.247. Absorption beyond 15 minutes not tested. 11 of 50 EIA reports produced significant return jumps; only 1 jump in the API window.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: The impact of crude oil inventory surprises in EIA report is almost twice the impact of the surprise in API reports. | In total, 11 out of 50 EIA reports generated significant return jumps.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: EIA response is immediate, effects last about 25 minutes, then the price reverts quickly
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: WTI futures around EIA reports (period not in abstract)
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Geman and Li, Journal of Energy Markets (E.20 gives 11(2), 2018; volume and year not shown on the IDEAS page), 'An analysis of intraday market response to crude oil inventory shocks'. Abstract only. Volatility and volume elevated about 25 minutes; price effect reverts quickly (reversal, not drift). Also a pre-release move 10:20-10:25 strategy (see T6 item 31).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: Market activity, in terms of price return, volatility and trading volume, responds to inventory shock very quickly, with the effects lasting for about twenty-five minutes. Our results suggest that a positive (negative) inventory shock will result in an immediate price decline (rise), while both kinds of shock increase volatility and trading volume; however, the price reverts quickly after the initial reaction.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: US macro releases (nonfarm payrolls, retail sales, others at 8:30 and 10:00 ET) cause oil-futures jumps; response 'very rapid'

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: employment situation report plays a key role, with more than 30% of the announcements on the change in nonfarm payrolls followed by jumps in oil prices. | oil prices respond very rapidly to new economic data

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: EIA crude-inventory shock does not predict nearby K-LRVK returns after the release (10:35-11:00 and 11:00-15:00 ET); it does predict returns in the 30 minutes and overnight before (leakage)

Text from a Firecrawl directQuote extraction of the PDF (raw PDF blocked by Cloudflare).

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Elder, Miao and Ramchander, Journal of Banking & Finance 2012 (repository version June 7, 2011; reused E.28 file). Absorption: return response mainly in 08:30-08:35 for gold and silver; copper shows a somewhat delayed response to 08:30 news; for 09:15 releases the peak R-square for gold and silver comes about 30 minutes later; for 10:00 releases a 5-10 minute delay in silver's peak; the response dissipates in less than an hour. Volatility effect decays within about 10 minutes. Authors call the response swift and the metals efficient.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Elder, Miao and Ramchander, Journal of Banking & Finance 2012 (repository version June 7, 2011; reused E.28 file). Absorption: return response mainly in 08:30-08:35 for gold and silver; copper shows a somewhat delayed response to 08:30 news; for 09:15 releases the peak R-square for gold and silver comes about 30 minutes later; for 10:00 releases a 5-10 minute delay in silver's peak; the response dissipates in less than an hour. Volatility effect decays within about 10 minutes. Authors call the response swift and the metals efficient.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: Notably, during the 8:30-8:35 minute interval, the highest adjusted R- square values are found for gold and silver. In contrast, copper exhibits a somewhat delayed response to the 8:30 announcement. For the 9:15 announcements, there is about a 30-minute delay before the realization of the highest adjusted R-square for gold and silver. ... about a 5-10 minute delay in the peak response of silver prices. In all cases, we observe that the metal prices are efficient in incorporating new economic information and the response tends to dissipate in less than an hour after the release of the announcement.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: US macro releases 08:30 ET (nonfarm payrolls, durable goods largest), 09:15 ET and 10:00 ET sets; monthly or less frequent
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: 2002-01 to 2008-12, 5-minute returns, K-LGJM K-AAUT K-YBWI futures
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Elder, Miao and Ramchander, Journal of Banking & Finance 2012 (repository version June 7, 2011; reused E.28 file). Absorption: return response mainly in 08:30-08:35 for gold and silver; copper shows a somewhat delayed response to 08:30 news; for 09:15 releases the peak R-square for gold and silver comes about 30 minutes later; for 10:00 releases a 5-10 minute delay in silver's peak; the response dissipates in less than an hour. Volatility effect decays within about 10 minutes. Authors call the response swift and the metals efficient.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: Notably, during the 8:30-8:35 minute interval, the highest adjusted R- square values are found for gold and silver. In contrast, copper exhibits a somewhat delayed response to the 8:30 announcement. For the 9:15 announcements, there is about a 30-minute delay before the realization of the highest adjusted R-square for gold and silver. ... about a 5-10 minute delay in the peak response of silver prices. In all cases, we observe that the metal prices are efficient in incorporating new economic information and the response tends to dissipate in less than an hour after the release of the announcement.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: US macro releases 08:30 ET (nonfarm payrolls, durable goods largest), 09:15 ET and 10:00 ET sets; monthly or less frequent
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: 2002-01 to 2008-12, 5-minute returns, K-LGJM K-AAUT K-YBWI futures
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Elder, Miao and Ramchander, Journal of Banking & Finance 2012 (repository version June 7, 2011; reused E.28 file). Absorption: return response mainly in 08:30-08:35 for gold and silver; copper shows a somewhat delayed response to 08:30 news; for 09:15 releases the peak R-square for gold and silver comes about 30 minutes later; for 10:00 releases a 5-10 minute delay in silver's peak; the response dissipates in less than an hour. Volatility effect decays within about 10 minutes. Authors call the response swift and the metals efficient.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: Notably, during the 8:30-8:35 minute interval, the highest adjusted R- square values are found for gold and silver. In contrast, copper exhibits a somewhat delayed response to the 8:30 announcement. For the 9:15 announcements, there is about a 30-minute delay before the realization of the highest adjusted R-square for gold and silver. ... about a 5-10 minute delay in the peak response of silver prices. In all cases, we observe that the metal prices are efficient in incorporating new economic information and the response tends to dissipate in less than an hour after the release of the announcement.

D3_s1_relationships.detail: Economic cross-asset pair, spot AUD/USD (not CME futures). Multi-horizon Granger causality at 5-minute and daily frequency: causality both ways, stronger at short horizons, commodity -> exchange rate dominant (ratios up to 5 or 10). D3_s1_relationships.quote: relation- ships exist contemporaneously, but fail to exhibit Granger-causality in either direction.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Absorption: conditional mean adjusts quickly ('effectively amounting to jumps'); variance adjusts gradually. D6_directional_evidence.applies_to: another venue of the same underlying
D6_directional_evidence.value: positive: intraday momentum and intraday reversal in Bitcoin, also in Ethereum; timing strategy beats buy-and-hold
D6_directional_evidence.window: Bitcoin high-frequency data 2013-03-03 to 2020-05-31 (venue not in abstract)
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Wen, Bouri, Xu and Zhao (2022), 'Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both', North American Journal of Economics and Finance 62, 101733 (peer-reviewed). Abstract only (IDEAS page). Horizons, OOS and cost treatment not in the abstract. Patterns change with jumps, FOMC releases, liquidity.
D6_directional_evidence.quote: Using high-frequency price data on Bitcoin from March 3, 2013, to May 31, 2020, it shows that the patterns of intraday return predictability change in the presence of large intraday price jumps, FOMC announcement release, liquidity levels, and the outbreak of the COVID-19. Intraday return predictability is also found in other actively traded cryptocurrencies such as Ethereum, Litecoin, and Ripple. Further analysis shows that the timing strategy based on the intraday predictors produces higher economic value than the benchmark strategy such as the always-long or the buy-and-hold.

D6_directional_evidence.quote: The predictability of high frequency returns varied over time. For most of the time, the cryptocurrencies were unpredictable. Nevertheless, their weak-form efficiency appeared to decrease along with an increase in frequency.

D6_directional_evidence.window: Bitcoin high-frequency data 2013-03-03 to 2020-05-31 (venue not in abstract)
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Wen, Bouri, Xu and Zhao (2022), 'Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both', North American Journal of Economics and Finance 62, 101733 (peer-reviewed). Abstract only (IDEAS page). Horizons, OOS and cost treatment not in the abstract. Patterns change with jumps, FOMC releases, liquidity.
D6_directional_evidence.quote: Using high-frequency price data on Bitcoin from March 3, 2013, to May 31, 2020, it shows that the patterns of intraday return predictability change in the presence of large intraday price jumps, FOMC announcement release, liquidity levels, and the outbreak of the COVID-19. Intraday return predictability is also found in other actively traded cryptocurrencies such as Ethereum, Litecoin, and Ripple. Further analysis shows that the timing strategy based on the intraday predictors produces higher economic value than the benchmark strategy such as the always-long or the buy-and-hold.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: CME K-ZXJD Hasbrouck IS 0.52-0.56 on 4 of 5 days; 0.13-0.15 on 2024-08-05 (Binance spot 0.84-0.87)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: five single days in 2024: Mar 5, Apr 30, May 20, Aug 5, Sep 6; K-ZXJD (CME) vs Binance K-OJGY spot, tick and 1-second data
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Working paper (arXiv 2506.08718, Plazuelo Pascual, Tardon Rubio, Toro Cebada, Hernando Veciana; ARFIMA Consulting and UC3M, 2025). Futures 'lead more often, although not as decisively'; Gonzalo-Granger 'Neither' on 4 days, 'Spot' on Aug 5; Hayashi-Yoshida lead-lag of 0.055-0.15 s for futures on 4 days. Mixed: neither market reaches 75% except spot on Aug 5. Note: K-ZXJD daily settles off K-OJGY, but this study uses K-ZXJD intraday prices.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: Table 3.36 ... March 0.563 Yes Neither 1.11 0.055 Yes / April 0.552 Yes Neither 1.15 0.066 Yes / May 0.521 Yes Neither 1.36 0.063 Yes / August 0.158 No Spot 0.97 -0.571 No / September 0.539 Yes Neither 1.94 0.15 Yes ... the futures market appears to lead more often, although not as decisively as in the centralized versus decentralized case. ... The futures data come from the CME [size class] K-OJGY (K-ZXJD)

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: spot leads CME and CBOE K-OJGY
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: from Dec 2017 launch (sample end not in abstract)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Baur and Dimpfl (2019), Journal of Futures Markets 39(7), peer-reviewed; Hasbrouck IS and Gonzalo-Granger. Shares not in the abstract.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: We rely on the information share methodology of Hasbrouck (1995 ...) and Gonzalo and Granger (1995 ...) and find that the spot price leads the futures price. We attribute this result to the higher trading volume and the longer trading hours of the globally distributed bitcoin spot market

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: CME leads price discovery (vs four settlement spot exchanges)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Aleti and Mizrach (2021), Journal of Futures Markets 41(2); also 'K-OJGY leads Ethereum price adjustment'. Shares not in the abstract. Full text (SSRN 3459111) not retrievable (SSRN blocks).
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: We study Bitcoin (K-OJGY) trading at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) and four settlement spot exchanges ... The CME leads price discovery. K-OJGY leads Ethereum price adjustment.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: time-varying contributions of spot and futures; driven by relative trading costs and volume
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Entrop, Frijns and Seruset (2020), Journal of Futures Markets 40; macro news has no impact on price discovery shares.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: Over the period December 2017–March 2019, we find significant time variation in the contribution to price discovery of the two markets. Increases in price discovery are mainly driven by relative trading costs and volume ... attention and macroeconomic news have no impact on price discovery.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: futures generally lead spot at 1-second sampling, with daily fluctuations; futures' share rises around macro surprises
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Frino, Gaudiosi, Webb and Zhou (2025), 'Price discovery in Bitcoin spot or futures? The jury is out', Journal of Futures Markets 45(4) 269-288; attributes earlier conflicts to measures, sampling frequency, windows, contracts and spot exchanges.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: Using 1-s sampling frequencies ... we find that the futures market generally leads spot markets, though this price leadership exhibits daily fluctuations. Moreover, we observe a pronounced increase in the futures market's contribution to price discovery around macroeconomic surprises and Tether stablecoin minting tweets.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: Kapar and Olmo (2019): futures dominate price discovery (Dec 2017 - May 2018); Alexander and Heck (2020): CME futures have a very minor effect, less than spot exchanges and offshore perpetuals
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: Kapar-Olmo Dec 2017 - May 2018; Alexander-Heck window not seen
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Both known only from search-result snippets: Kapar-Olmo's Southampton eprint returned web 401 and the araid.es page 404; Alexander-Heck (J. Financial Stability 2020) is on SSRN (blocked). Not verified.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: [snippet] Kapar and Olmo (2019): Using Hasbrouck's information share and Gonzalo and Granger's common factor component on December 2017 to May 2018 data, they conclude the futures market dominates price discovery. ... Alexander and Heck (2020, SSRN): ... CME futures have a very minor effect on price discovery, even less than the spot exchanges Bitfinex, Bitstamp and Coinbase.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: K-ZXJD's information share approximately equal to or slightly greater than K-OJGY's (Hasbrouck IS and Lien-Shrestha modified IS); exact shares not in abstract
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: intraday; period not in abstract (K-ZXJD launched 2021-05-03; published 2022)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Pati (2022), 'Informativeness of CME [size class] K-OJGY in Pricing of Bitcoin: Intraday Evidence', Finance Research Letters 49, 103084 (peer-reviewed). Abstract only (IDEAS). Relevant to the Sat (iii) test: on this abstract K-ZXJD is not attributed 75% or more of discovery to K-OJGY (approximately equal), but no number is given. Full text paywalled.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: Hasbrouck's information share, and Lien and Shrestha's modified information share suggest that K-ZXJD contributes approximately equal or slightly greater proportion to price discovery with K-OJGY. The dominance of K-ZXJD is marginally higher in Bitstamp and itBit compared to Coinbase and Kraken.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: K-OJGY dominate price discovery relative to spot; CBOE futures led CME's
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: period surrounding the Dec 2017 futures launches (high-frequency data)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Akyildirim, Corbet, Katsiampa, Kellard and Sensoy (2020), 'The development of K-OJGY: exploring the interactions between cryptocurrency derivatives', Finance Research Letters (peer-reviewed). Abstract only (Bilkent repository record). CBOE K-OJGY delisted later (not in the abstract). Shares not given.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: we verify the view that K-OJGY dominate price discovery relative to spot markets. However, we add to this research by finding that CBOE futures are found to be the leading source of informational flow when compared directly to their CME equivalent.

D6_directional_evidence.value: positive: intraday momentum and intraday reversal in Bitcoin, also in Ethereum; timing strategy beats buy-and-hold
D6_directional_evidence.window: Bitcoin high-frequency data 2013-03-03 to 2020-05-31 (venue not in abstract)
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Wen, Bouri, Xu and Zhao (2022), 'Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both', North American Journal of Economics and Finance 62, 101733 (peer-reviewed). Abstract only (IDEAS page). Horizons, OOS and cost treatment not in the abstract. Patterns change with jumps, FOMC releases, liquidity.
D6_directional_evidence.quote: Using high-frequency price data on Bitcoin from March 3, 2013, to May 31, 2020, it shows that the patterns of intraday return predictability change in the presence of large intraday price jumps, FOMC announcement release, liquidity levels, and the outbreak of the COVID-19. Intraday return predictability is also found in other actively traded cryptocurrencies such as Ethereum, Litecoin, and Ripple. Further analysis shows that the timing strategy based on the intraday predictors produces higher economic value than the benchmark strategy such as the always-long or the buy-and-hold.

Venue of the Bitcoin price series not grep-checked. Absorption speed: not applicable (no effect found).

In separate analysis (available upon request), we also consider a one-hour interval, from five minutes before the event to fifty-five minutes after, and the main results continue to hold. ... for all assets except Bitcoin, which is based on the sample January 2017 - December 2022.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: CME K-ZXJD Hasbrouck IS 0.52-0.56 on 4 of 5 days; 0.13-0.15 on 2024-08-05 (Binance spot 0.84-0.87)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: five single days in 2024: Mar 5, Apr 30, May 20, Aug 5, Sep 6; K-ZXJD (CME) vs Binance K-OJGY spot, tick and 1-second data
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Working paper (arXiv 2506.08718, Plazuelo Pascual, Tardon Rubio, Toro Cebada, Hernando Veciana; ARFIMA Consulting and UC3M, 2025). Futures 'lead more often, although not as decisively'; Gonzalo-Granger 'Neither' on 4 days, 'Spot' on Aug 5; Hayashi-Yoshida lead-lag of 0.055-0.15 s for futures on 4 days. Mixed: neither market reaches 75% except spot on Aug 5. Note: K-ZXJD daily settles off K-OJGY, but this study uses K-ZXJD intraday prices.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: Table 3.36 ... March 0.563 Yes Neither 1.11 0.055 Yes / April 0.552 Yes Neither 1.15 0.066 Yes / May 0.521 Yes Neither 1.36 0.063 Yes / August 0.158 No Spot 0.97 -0.571 No / September 0.539 Yes Neither 1.94 0.15 Yes ... the futures market appears to lead more often, although not as decisively as in the centralized versus decentralized case. ... The futures data come from the CME [size class] K-OJGY (K-ZXJD)

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: spot leads CME and CBOE K-OJGY
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: from Dec 2017 launch (sample end not in abstract)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Baur and Dimpfl (2019), Journal of Futures Markets 39(7), peer-reviewed; Hasbrouck IS and Gonzalo-Granger. Shares not in the abstract.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: We rely on the information share methodology of Hasbrouck (1995 ...) and Gonzalo and Granger (1995 ...) and find that the spot price leads the futures price. We attribute this result to the higher trading volume and the longer trading hours of the globally distributed bitcoin spot market

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: CME leads price discovery (vs four settlement spot exchanges)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Aleti and Mizrach (2021), Journal of Futures Markets 41(2); also 'K-OJGY leads Ethereum price adjustment'. Shares not in the abstract. Full text (SSRN 3459111) not retrievable (SSRN blocks).
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: We study Bitcoin (K-OJGY) trading at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) and four settlement spot exchanges ... The CME leads price discovery. K-OJGY leads Ethereum price adjustment.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: time-varying contributions of spot and futures; driven by relative trading costs and volume
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Entrop, Frijns and Seruset (2020), Journal of Futures Markets 40; macro news has no impact on price discovery shares.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: Over the period December 2017–March 2019, we find significant time variation in the contribution to price discovery of the two markets. Increases in price discovery are mainly driven by relative trading costs and volume ... attention and macroeconomic news have no impact on price discovery.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: futures generally lead spot at 1-second sampling, with daily fluctuations; futures' share rises around macro surprises
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Frino, Gaudiosi, Webb and Zhou (2025), 'Price discovery in Bitcoin spot or futures? The jury is out', Journal of Futures Markets 45(4) 269-288; attributes earlier conflicts to measures, sampling frequency, windows, contracts and spot exchanges.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: Using 1-s sampling frequencies ... we find that the futures market generally leads spot markets, though this price leadership exhibits daily fluctuations. Moreover, we observe a pronounced increase in the futures market's contribution to price discovery around macroeconomic surprises and Tether stablecoin minting tweets.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: Kapar and Olmo (2019): futures dominate price discovery (Dec 2017 - May 2018); Alexander and Heck (2020): CME futures have a very minor effect, less than spot exchanges and offshore perpetuals
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: Kapar-Olmo Dec 2017 - May 2018; Alexander-Heck window not seen
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Both known only from search-result snippets: Kapar-Olmo's Southampton eprint returned web 401 and the araid.es page 404; Alexander-Heck (J. Financial Stability 2020) is on SSRN (blocked). Not verified.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: [snippet] Kapar and Olmo (2019): Using Hasbrouck's information share and Gonzalo and Granger's common factor component on December 2017 to May 2018 data, they conclude the futures market dominates price discovery. ... Alexander and Heck (2020, SSRN): ... CME futures have a very minor effect on price discovery, even less than the spot exchanges Bitfinex, Bitstamp and Coinbase.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: K-ZXJD's information share approximately equal to or slightly greater than K-OJGY's (Hasbrouck IS and Lien-Shrestha modified IS); exact shares not in abstract
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: intraday; period not in abstract (K-ZXJD launched 2021-05-03; published 2022)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Pati (2022), 'Informativeness of CME [size class] K-OJGY in Pricing of Bitcoin: Intraday Evidence', Finance Research Letters 49, 103084 (peer-reviewed). Abstract only (IDEAS). Relevant to the Sat (iii) test: on this abstract K-ZXJD is not attributed 75% or more of discovery to K-OJGY (approximately equal), but no number is given. Full text paywalled.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: Hasbrouck's information share, and Lien and Shrestha's modified information share suggest that K-ZXJD contributes approximately equal or slightly greater proportion to price discovery with K-OJGY. The dominance of K-ZXJD is marginally higher in Bitstamp and itBit compared to Coinbase and Kraken.

Sat_iii_price_discovery.value: K-OJGY dominate price discovery relative to spot; CBOE futures led CME's
Sat_iii_price_discovery.window: period surrounding the Dec 2017 futures launches (high-frequency data)
Sat_iii_price_discovery.detail: Akyildirim, Corbet, Katsiampa, Kellard and Sensoy (2020), 'The development of K-OJGY: exploring the interactions between cryptocurrency derivatives', Finance Research Letters (peer-reviewed). Abstract only (Bilkent repository record). CBOE K-OJGY delisted later (not in the abstract). Shares not given.
Sat_iii_price_discovery.quote: we verify the view that K-OJGY dominate price discovery relative to spot markets. However, we add to this research by finding that CBOE futures are found to be the leading source of informational flow when compared directly to their CME equivalent.

D6_directional_evidence.window: Bitcoin high-frequency data 2013-03-03 to 2020-05-31 (venue not in abstract)
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Wen, Bouri, Xu and Zhao (2022), 'Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both', North American Journal of Economics and Finance 62, 101733 (peer-reviewed). D6_directional_evidence.quote: Using high-frequency price data on Bitcoin from March 3, 2013, to May 31, 2020, it shows that the patterns of intraday return predictability change in the presence of large intraday price jumps, FOMC announcement release, liquidity levels, and the outbreak of the COVID-19. Intraday return predictability is also found in other actively traded cryptocurrencies such as Ethereum, Litecoin, and Ripple. Further analysis shows that the timing strategy based on the intraday predictors produces higher economic value than the benchmark strategy such as the always-long or the buy-and-hold.

D6_directional_evidence.value: market intraday momentum, equity: positive, significant (pooled, full sample)
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (2021) JFE 142(1), peer-reviewed. 17 developed-market equity index futures. Signal r_ROD = return from previous day's close to 30 min before today's close; target r_LH = last 30 min before the close (horizon 30 min, entry at close-30). Closes are the underlying cash close for equity futures (09:30-16:00 ET for US index futures), volume-spike times for others. In-sample pooled/individual OLS plus a recursive expanding-window out-of-sample R2 (min 500 obs) with a Clark-West test; trading results NOT net of costs. Data: Tick Data LLC one-minute bars. Table 2 Panel A (l.975-978): beta_ROD 4.18*** (t 7.29), R2 2.45%, R2_OOS 2.88%. Table 5 Panel B 2000-2020 (l.1626): beta_ROD 3.98*** (t 6.65), R2 2.34%. Table 6 Panel A: eta(r_ROD) 1/N portfolio SR 1.73, ann. ret 6.86%, success 0.55 (gross). Table B1 Panel A USA group: beta_ROD 5.99*** (t 6.66), R2_OOS 3.09%.

D6_directional_evidence.value: market intraday momentum, equity: positive, significant (pooled, full sample)
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (2021) JFE 142(1), peer-reviewed. 17 developed-market equity index futures. Signal r_ROD = return from previous day's close to 30 min before today's close; target r_LH = last 30 min before the close (horizon 30 min, entry at close-30). Closes are the underlying cash close for equity futures (09:30-16:00 ET for US index futures), volume-spike times for others. In-sample pooled/individual OLS plus a recursive expanding-window out-of-sample R2 (min 500 obs) with a Clark-West test; trading results NOT net of costs. Data: Tick Data LLC one-minute bars. Table 2 Panel A (l.975-978): beta_ROD 4.18*** (t 7.29), R2 2.45%, R2_OOS 2.88%. Table 5 Panel B 2000-2020 (l.1626): beta_ROD 3.98*** (t 6.65), R2 2.34%. Table 6 Panel A: eta(r_ROD) 1/N portfolio SR 1.73, ann. ret 6.86%, success 0.55 (gross). Table B1 Panel A USA group: beta_ROD 5.99*** (t 6.66), R2_OOS 3.09%.

D6_directional_evidence.quote: This study examines the intraday price patterns in the U.S. Treasury note futures market. Significantly negative serial correlations of price changes have been found throughout the trading day. The serial correlations are consistently negative throughout the trading day and have declined considerably over time. In addition, it is seen that the level of recent daily serial correlations is predictive of correlations throughout the trading day. A trading strategy has been tested based on these results and shows that excess profits can be earned. Importantly, the trading results are seen to improve when the level of serial correlation is used to refine the trading strategy.

D6_directional_evidence.quote: This study examines the intraday price patterns in the U.S. Treasury note futures market. Significantly negative serial correlations of price changes have been found throughout the trading day. The serial correlations are consistently negative throughout the trading day and have declined considerably over time. In addition, it is seen that the level of recent daily serial correlations is predictive of correlations throughout the trading day. A trading strategy has been tested based on these results and shows that excess profits can be earned. Importantly, the trading results are seen to improve when the level of serial correlation is used to refine the trading strategy.

D6_directional_evidence.quote: This study examines the intraday price patterns in the U.S. Treasury note futures market. Significantly negative serial correlations of price changes have been found throughout the trading day. The serial correlations are consistently negative throughout the trading day and have declined considerably over time. In addition, it is seen that the level of recent daily serial correlations is predictive of correlations throughout the trading day. A trading strategy has been tested based on these results and shows that excess profits can be earned. Importantly, the trading results are seen to improve when the level of serial correlation is used to refine the trading strategy.

D6_directional_evidence.window: not stated in abstract; published 2009 (pre-2010 data)
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Cusatis, Kulkarni, Thomas (2009), 'Intraday serial correlation and the predictability of returns in the U.S. treasury note futures market', Banking and Finance Review (PSU Pure abstract page). Horizon, maturity, sample and costs not in the abstract. Correlations 'have declined considerably over time'.
D6_directional_evidence.quote: This study examines the intraday price patterns in the U.S. Treasury note futures market. Significantly negative serial correlations of price changes have been found throughout the trading day. The serial correlations are consistently negative throughout the trading day and have declined considerably over time. In addition, it is seen that the level of recent daily serial correlations is predictive of correlations throughout the trading day. A trading strategy has been tested based on these results and shows that excess profits can be earned. Importantly, the trading results are seen to improve when the level of serial correlation is used to refine the trading strategy.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: WASDE (monthly, 12:00 ET since 2013): price effect not significant at 10 min, significant at 30 min; soybean reaction keeps growing from 30 min to the day close
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: 2010-2021, 122 WASDE reports, CME nearby corn and K-IXHJ
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Anderson, McKenzie, Noyes (2024) NCCC-134 conference paper (working paper, not peer-reviewed). Event study: return from release (or from the open when released before the open) to +10 min, +30 min and the day close, regressed on WASDE world-ending-stocks surprise vs Bloomberg analyst survey (SUR). Corn: -0.023 (10 min, n.s.), -0.041** (30 min), -0.044* (day). Soybeans: -0.028 (n.s.), -0.061**, -0.124** (day); 10-min vs day coefficients differ significantly for soybeans only. Absorption: slow for soybeans (drift beyond 30 min, surprise-conditional, in sample); corn mostly done by 30 min. Needs the analyst-survey surprise. Contradicts Lehecka et al. 2014 (about 10 min) and Adjemian-Irwin 2018 (few minutes).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: We do not find a significant market reaction within the first ten minutes after the report release time. However, we do find significant and directionally appropriate price reactions after 30 minutes. Furthermore, the price reaction continues to grow for soybeans between 30 minutes and the daily close.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: major USDA reports: reactions persist about ten minutes; no systematic under- or overreaction
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Lehecka, Wang, Garcia (2014) Applied Economic Perspectives and Policy 36(3) 504-526 (peer-reviewed). D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: Strongest price reactions to the releases are found immediately after the market opens, and market reactions persist for approximately ten minutes. The electronic K-OQCY market quickly incorporates this new public information, and little evidence exists to support systematic under- or overreactions in prices.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: ensuing real-time trading on USDA crop announcements exhibits noticeable volatility spikes in agricultural futures markets, but that this heightened volatility dissipates within the space of a few trading minutes.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: WASDE (monthly, 12:00 ET since 2013): price effect not significant at 10 min, significant at 30 min; soybean reaction keeps growing from 30 min to the day close
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: 2010-2021, 122 WASDE reports, CME nearby corn and K-IXHJ
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Anderson, McKenzie, Noyes (2024) NCCC-134 conference paper (working paper, not peer-reviewed). Event study: return from release (or from the open when released before the open) to +10 min, +30 min and the day close, regressed on WASDE world-ending-stocks surprise vs Bloomberg analyst survey (SUR). Corn: -0.023 (10 min, n.s.), -0.041** (30 min), -0.044* (day). Soybeans: -0.028 (n.s.), -0.061**, -0.124** (day); 10-min vs day coefficients differ significantly for soybeans only. Absorption: slow for soybeans (drift beyond 30 min, surprise-conditional, in sample); corn mostly done by 30 min. Needs the analyst-survey surprise. Contradicts Lehecka et al. 2014 (about 10 min) and Adjemian-Irwin 2018 (few minutes).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: We do not find a significant market reaction within the first ten minutes after the report release time. However, we do find significant and directionally appropriate price reactions after 30 minutes. Furthermore, the price reaction continues to grow for soybeans between 30 minutes and the daily close.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: ensuing real-time trading on USDA crop announcements exhibits noticeable volatility spikes in agricultural futures markets, but that this heightened volatility dissipates within the space of a few trading minutes.

D6_directional_evidence.value: first half-hour return positively predicts last half-hour return: DCE soybean slope 0.073 (R2 1.80%), soybean meal slope 0.052 (R2 0.90%), significant at 5%
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Jin, Kearney, Li, Yang, 'Intraday time-series momentum: Evidence from China', Journal of Futures Markets (2019/2020, peer-reviewed; doi 10.1002/fut.22084); MPRA working paper 97134 (Nov 2019) read in full. Venue: Dalian Commodity Exchange (another venue of the K-IXHJ and K-KQRO underlyings). Horizon: first 30 min -> last 30 min of the day; also rest-of-day. In sample (full-sample regressions); trading-strategy returns GROSS of transaction costs. Sign positive (momentum). Only the second-to-last session also predicts for soybean meal; overnight return has power for soybean meal. Data mostly before 2010-2013.
D6_directional_evidence.quote: We observe that the first 30-minute returns positively predict the last 30-minute returns for all four contracts with a slope of 0.073 for soybean, 0.052 for soybean meal, 0.067 for copper, and 0.103 for steel. All of these are significant at a 5% level. Furthermore, the R2 for these four contracts are 1.80%, 0.90% 1.36% and 3.32%, respectively. ... The returns comparison presented in Table 7 is based on gross returns that do not take transaction costs into account.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush (K-IXHJ vs K-KQRO and K-ODAS): intraday cointegration at 1-minute sampling in the day session
D3_s1_relationships.window: calendar 2015, 243 trading days, CME LOB data
D3_s1_relationships.detail: Type: economic spread. Zhou, Bagnarosa, Gohin, Pennings, Debie (2023) J. Commodity Markets 30, 100314 (peer-reviewed; open-access copy). Day session (08:30-13:20 CT, 'session 2'), 1-minute data, missing-data filtered: cointegrated on 180 of 243 days (Table 2), 229 days at 2-minute sampling (NCCC-134 2022 version); Johansen without filtering only 64-70 days. Overnight 'session 1' (19:00-07:45 CT): 52 days (NCCC version Table 7). Speed of reversion related to volume and liquidity; stronger cointegration on USDA days. Horizon: minute-level, within-day. No half-life or trading test reported. In sample.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: A high level of cointegration is indeed observed during session 2 trading hours, which fades away during session 1. Another interesting result is the stronger intraday cointegration observed on average on USDA announcement days, although the number of observations available is limited.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush: overnight session cointegration on 52 days vs 180 in the day session (1-minute, 2015)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: NCCC-134 2022 conference version of [ref] (working paper). Table 7 'Cointegration Summary of Session 1': K-IXHJ open interest rollover 52 days, 2 months, 1 quarter. Two-minute data: 229 cointegrated days in session 2.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: cointegration is mainly playing during session 2 (market official trading hours) of a trading day and significantly less so during session 1 (electronic trading hours). In addition, prices in session 1 are so greatly affected by market noise that even the combining of both sessions yields no additional information

D3_s1_relationships.quote: Liquidity persistence and positive liquidity spillovers mainly occur within 30 s, whereas spillovers for longer horizons are mostly negative. Findings are important for hedgers that hedge the crush and traders who wish to capitalize on the short-term deviation of price relationships.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush (K-IXHJ vs K-KQRO and K-ODAS): intraday cointegration at 1-minute sampling in the day session
D3_s1_relationships.window: calendar 2015, 243 trading days, CME LOB data
D3_s1_relationships.detail: Type: economic spread. Zhou, Bagnarosa, Gohin, Pennings, Debie (2023) J. Commodity Markets 30, 100314 (peer-reviewed; open-access copy). Day session (08:30-13:20 CT, 'session 2'), 1-minute data, missing-data filtered: cointegrated on 180 of 243 days (Table 2), 229 days at 2-minute sampling (NCCC-134 2022 version); Johansen without filtering only 64-70 days. Overnight 'session 1' (19:00-07:45 CT): 52 days (NCCC version Table 7). Speed of reversion related to volume and liquidity; stronger cointegration on USDA days. Horizon: minute-level, within-day. No half-life or trading test reported. In sample.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: A high level of cointegration is indeed observed during session 2 trading hours, which fades away during session 1. Another interesting result is the stronger intraday cointegration observed on average on USDA announcement days, although the number of observations available is limited.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush: overnight session cointegration on 52 days vs 180 in the day session (1-minute, 2015)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: NCCC-134 2022 conference version of [ref] (working paper). Table 7 'Cointegration Summary of Session 1': K-IXHJ open interest rollover 52 days, 2 months, 1 quarter. Two-minute data: 229 cointegrated days in session 2.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: cointegration is mainly playing during session 2 (market official trading hours) of a trading day and significantly less so during session 1 (electronic trading hours). In addition, prices in session 1 are so greatly affected by market noise that even the combining of both sessions yields no additional information

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean complex liquidity: persistence and positive cross-market spillovers mainly within 30 s; negative at longer horizons
D3_s1_relationships.window: CME soybean complex LOB (2015 per planner pointer, unverified)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: de Boer, Gardebroek, Pennings, Trujillo-Barrera (2022) J. Futures Markets (peer-reviewed). Liquidity, not returns: not evidence of price mean reversion. Planner pointer (unverified): round-trip liquidity cost 9.2 bp K-IXHJ, 12.5 bp K-ODAS, 13.6 bp K-KQRO. Abstract only.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: Liquidity persistence and positive liquidity spillovers mainly occur within 30 s, whereas spillovers for longer horizons are mostly negative. Findings are important for hedgers that hedge the crush and traders who wish to capitalize on the short-term deviation of price relationships.

D6_directional_evidence.value: first half-hour return positively predicts last half-hour return: DCE soybean slope 0.073 (R2 1.80%), soybean meal slope 0.052 (R2 0.90%), significant at 5%
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Jin, Kearney, Li, Yang, 'Intraday time-series momentum: Evidence from China', Journal of Futures Markets (2019/2020, peer-reviewed; doi 10.1002/fut.22084); MPRA working paper 97134 (Nov 2019) read in full. Venue: Dalian Commodity Exchange (another venue of the K-IXHJ and K-KQRO underlyings). Horizon: first 30 min -> last 30 min of the day; also rest-of-day. In sample (full-sample regressions); trading-strategy returns GROSS of transaction costs. Sign positive (momentum). Only the second-to-last session also predicts for soybean meal; overnight return has power for soybean meal. Data mostly before 2010-2013.
D6_directional_evidence.quote: We observe that the first 30-minute returns positively predict the last 30-minute returns for all four contracts with a slope of 0.073 for soybean, 0.052 for soybean meal, 0.067 for copper, and 0.103 for steel. All of these are significant at a 5% level. Furthermore, the R2 for these four contracts are 1.80%, 0.90% 1.36% and 3.32%, respectively. ... The returns comparison presented in Table 7 is based on gross returns that do not take transaction costs into account.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: WASDE (monthly, 12:00 ET since 2013): price effect not significant at 10 min, significant at 30 min; soybean reaction keeps growing from 30 min to the day close
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: 2010-2021, 122 WASDE reports, CME nearby corn and K-IXHJ
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Anderson, McKenzie, Noyes (2024) NCCC-134 conference paper (working paper, not peer-reviewed). Event study: return from release (or from the open when released before the open) to +10 min, +30 min and the day close, regressed on WASDE world-ending-stocks surprise vs Bloomberg analyst survey (SUR). Corn: -0.023 (10 min, n.s.), -0.041** (30 min), -0.044* (day). Soybeans: -0.028 (n.s.), -0.061**, -0.124** (day); 10-min vs day coefficients differ significantly for soybeans only. Absorption: slow for soybeans (drift beyond 30 min, surprise-conditional, in sample); corn mostly done by 30 min. Needs the analyst-survey surprise. Contradicts Lehecka et al. 2014 (about 10 min) and Adjemian-Irwin 2018 (few minutes).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: We do not find a significant market reaction within the first ten minutes after the report release time. However, we do find significant and directionally appropriate price reactions after 30 minutes. Furthermore, the price reaction continues to grow for soybeans between 30 minutes and the daily close.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: major USDA reports: reactions persist about ten minutes; no systematic under- or overreaction

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: Strongest price reactions to the releases are found immediately after the market opens, and market reactions persist for approximately ten minutes. The electronic K-OQCY market quickly incorporates this new public information, and little evidence exists to support systematic under- or overreactions in prices.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush (K-IXHJ vs K-KQRO and K-ODAS): intraday cointegration at 1-minute sampling in the day session
D3_s1_relationships.window: calendar 2015, 243 trading days, CME LOB data
D3_s1_relationships.detail: Type: economic spread. Zhou, Bagnarosa, Gohin, Pennings, Debie (2023) J. Commodity Markets 30, 100314 (peer-reviewed; open-access copy). Day session (08:30-13:20 CT, 'session 2'), 1-minute data, missing-data filtered: cointegrated on 180 of 243 days (Table 2), 229 days at 2-minute sampling (NCCC-134 2022 version); Johansen without filtering only 64-70 days. Overnight 'session 1' (19:00-07:45 CT): 52 days (NCCC version Table 7). Speed of reversion related to volume and liquidity; stronger cointegration on USDA days. Horizon: minute-level, within-day. No half-life or trading test reported. In sample.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: A high level of cointegration is indeed observed during session 2 trading hours, which fades away during session 1. Another interesting result is the stronger intraday cointegration observed on average on USDA announcement days, although the number of observations available is limited.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush: overnight session cointegration on 52 days vs 180 in the day session (1-minute, 2015)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: NCCC-134 2022 conference version of [ref] (working paper). Table 7 'Cointegration Summary of Session 1': K-IXHJ open interest rollover 52 days, 2 months, 1 quarter. Two-minute data: 229 cointegrated days in session 2.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: cointegration is mainly playing during session 2 (market official trading hours) of a trading day and significantly less so during session 1 (electronic trading hours). In addition, prices in session 1 are so greatly affected by market noise that even the combining of both sessions yields no additional information

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean complex liquidity: persistence and positive cross-market spillovers mainly within 30 s; negative at longer horizons
D3_s1_relationships.window: CME soybean complex LOB (2015 per planner pointer, unverified)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: de Boer, Gardebroek, Pennings, Trujillo-Barrera (2022) J. Futures Markets (peer-reviewed). Liquidity, not returns: not evidence of price mean reversion. Planner pointer (unverified): round-trip liquidity cost 9.2 bp K-IXHJ, 12.5 bp K-ODAS, 13.6 bp K-KQRO. Abstract only.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: Liquidity persistence and positive liquidity spillovers mainly occur within 30 s, whereas spillovers for longer horizons are mostly negative. Findings are important for hedgers that hedge the crush and traders who wish to capitalize on the short-term deviation of price relationships.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: WASDE (monthly, 12:00 ET since 2013): price effect not significant at 10 min, significant at 30 min; soybean reaction keeps growing from 30 min to the day close
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: 2010-2021, 122 WASDE reports, CME nearby corn and K-IXHJ
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Anderson, McKenzie, Noyes (2024) NCCC-134 conference paper (working paper, not peer-reviewed). Event study: return from release (or from the open when released before the open) to +10 min, +30 min and the day close, regressed on WASDE world-ending-stocks surprise vs Bloomberg analyst survey (SUR). Corn: -0.023 (10 min, n.s.), -0.041** (30 min), -0.044* (day). Soybeans: -0.028 (n.s.), -0.061**, -0.124** (day); 10-min vs day coefficients differ significantly for soybeans only. Absorption: slow for soybeans (drift beyond 30 min, surprise-conditional, in sample); corn mostly done by 30 min. Needs the analyst-survey surprise. Contradicts Lehecka et al. 2014 (about 10 min) and Adjemian-Irwin 2018 (few minutes).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: We do not find a significant market reaction within the first ten minutes after the report release time. However, we do find significant and directionally appropriate price reactions after 30 minutes. Furthermore, the price reaction continues to grow for soybeans between 30 minutes and the daily close.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: ensuing real-time trading on USDA crop announcements exhibits noticeable volatility spikes in agricultural futures markets, but that this heightened volatility dissipates within the space of a few trading minutes.

D6_directional_evidence.value: first half-hour return positively predicts last half-hour return: DCE soybean slope 0.073 (R2 1.80%), soybean meal slope 0.052 (R2 0.90%), significant at 5%
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Jin, Kearney, Li, Yang, 'Intraday time-series momentum: Evidence from China', Journal of Futures Markets (2019/2020, peer-reviewed; doi 10.1002/fut.22084); MPRA working paper 97134 (Nov 2019) read in full. Venue: Dalian Commodity Exchange (another venue of the K-IXHJ and K-KQRO underlyings). Horizon: first 30 min -> last 30 min of the day; also rest-of-day. In sample (full-sample regressions); trading-strategy returns GROSS of transaction costs. Sign positive (momentum). Only the second-to-last session also predicts for soybean meal; overnight return has power for soybean meal. Data mostly before 2010-2013.
D6_directional_evidence.quote: We observe that the first 30-minute returns positively predict the last 30-minute returns for all four contracts with a slope of 0.073 for soybean, 0.052 for soybean meal, 0.067 for copper, and 0.103 for steel. All of these are significant at a 5% level. Furthermore, the R2 for these four contracts are 1.80%, 0.90% 1.36% and 3.32%, respectively. ... The returns comparison presented in Table 7 is based on gross returns that do not take transaction costs into account.

D3_s1_relationships.value: corn nearby vs deferred futures (calendar): intraday cointegration on about 70% of days; nearby price-discovery share 52% vs first deferred, 78% vs fourth deferred
D3_s1_relationships.window: 2008-2015, CME Top-of-Book transactions time-stamped to the second, daily estimation
D3_s1_relationships.detail: Hu, Mallory, Serra, Garcia (2017) working paper (arXiv 1711.03506; Univ. of Illinois). Type: calendar. Intraday (within-day) cointegration and Hasbrouck IS / component shares between nearby and deferred corn contracts. Nearby loses dominance when its relative volume share falls below 50%. In sample; not a trading test.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: The percentage of the days in which we reject the null hypothesis of no cointegration is about 70% across all contract pairs for both commodities, suggesting nearby and deferred futures share the same stochastic trend most of the time. ... For K-OQCY, the nearby contract only slightly dominates the first deferred contract in price discovery with an average price discovery share of 52%. ... By the deferred 4 contract, the nearby price discovery share has reached 78%.

D3_s1_relationships.value: corn, soybean and K-AJZH cointegrated at weekly frequency (two cointegrating vectors); trading rules with significant risk-adjusted returns
D3_s1_relationships.window: weekly prices (period in paper, not extracted); working paper 2012
D3_s1_relationships.detail: Arendarski and Postek (2012) University of Warsaw WNE Working Paper 2/2012 (68). Type: economic cross-commodity, documented only at weekly horizon (longer than daily). In sample estimation with out-of-sample stability tests; costs not checked here.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: Johansen tests indicate that natural logarithms of weekly prices of corn, soya and K-AJZH are cointegrated and two cointegrating vectors exist.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: WASDE (monthly, 12:00 ET since 2013): price effect not significant at 10 min, significant at 30 min; soybean reaction keeps growing from 30 min to the day close
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: 2010-2021, 122 WASDE reports, CME nearby corn and K-IXHJ
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Anderson, McKenzie, Noyes (2024) NCCC-134 conference paper (working paper, not peer-reviewed). Event study: return from release (or from the open when released before the open) to +10 min, +30 min and the day close, regressed on WASDE world-ending-stocks surprise vs Bloomberg analyst survey (SUR). Corn: -0.023 (10 min, n.s.), -0.041** (30 min), -0.044* (day). Soybeans: -0.028 (n.s.), -0.061**, -0.124** (day); 10-min vs day coefficients differ significantly for soybeans only. Absorption: slow for soybeans (drift beyond 30 min, surprise-conditional, in sample); corn mostly done by 30 min. Needs the analyst-survey surprise. Contradicts Lehecka et al. 2014 (about 10 min) and Adjemian-Irwin 2018 (few minutes).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: We do not find a significant market reaction within the first ten minutes after the report release time. However, we do find significant and directionally appropriate price reactions after 30 minutes. Furthermore, the price reaction continues to grow for soybeans between 30 minutes and the daily close.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: major USDA reports: reactions persist about ten minutes; no systematic under- or overreaction
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Lehecka, Wang, Garcia (2014) Applied Economic Perspectives and Policy 36(3) 504-526 (peer-reviewed). Absorption: within about 10 minutes (mostly before the 2013 move to 11:00 CT releases, when reports came out before the open). Negative for drift. Full text paywalled; abstract only.
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: Strongest price reactions to the releases are found immediately after the market opens, and market reactions persist for approximately ten minutes. The electronic K-OQCY market quickly incorporates this new public information, and little evidence exists to support systematic under- or overreactions in prices.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: ensuing real-time trading on USDA crop announcements exhibits noticeable volatility spikes in agricultural futures markets, but that this heightened volatility dissipates within the space of a few trading minutes.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush (K-IXHJ vs K-KQRO and K-ODAS): intraday cointegration at 1-minute sampling in the day session
D3_s1_relationships.window: calendar 2015, 243 trading days, CME LOB data
D3_s1_relationships.detail: Type: economic spread. Zhou, Bagnarosa, Gohin, Pennings, Debie (2023) J. Commodity Markets 30, 100314 (peer-reviewed; open-access copy). Day session (08:30-13:20 CT, 'session 2'), 1-minute data, missing-data filtered: cointegrated on 180 of 243 days (Table 2), 229 days at 2-minute sampling (NCCC-134 2022 version); Johansen without filtering only 64-70 days. Overnight 'session 1' (19:00-07:45 CT): 52 days (NCCC version Table 7). Speed of reversion related to volume and liquidity; stronger cointegration on USDA days. Horizon: minute-level, within-day. No half-life or trading test reported. In sample.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: A high level of cointegration is indeed observed during session 2 trading hours, which fades away during session 1. Another interesting result is the stronger intraday cointegration observed on average on USDA announcement days, although the number of observations available is limited.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush: overnight session cointegration on 52 days vs 180 in the day session (1-minute, 2015)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: NCCC-134 2022 conference version of [ref] (working paper). Table 7 'Cointegration Summary of Session 1': K-IXHJ open interest rollover 52 days, 2 months, 1 quarter. Two-minute data: 229 cointegrated days in session 2.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: cointegration is mainly playing during session 2 (market official trading hours) of a trading day and significantly less so during session 1 (electronic trading hours). In addition, prices in session 1 are so greatly affected by market noise that even the combining of both sessions yields no additional information

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean complex liquidity: persistence and positive cross-market spillovers mainly within 30 s; negative at longer horizons
D3_s1_relationships.window: CME soybean complex LOB (2015 per planner pointer, unverified)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: de Boer, Gardebroek, Pennings, Trujillo-Barrera (2022) J. Futures Markets (peer-reviewed). Liquidity, not returns: not evidence of price mean reversion. Planner pointer (unverified): round-trip liquidity cost 9.2 bp K-IXHJ, 12.5 bp K-ODAS, 13.6 bp K-KQRO. Abstract only.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: Liquidity persistence and positive liquidity spillovers mainly occur within 30 s, whereas spillovers for longer horizons are mostly negative. Findings are important for hedgers that hedge the crush and traders who wish to capitalize on the short-term deviation of price relationships.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.value: WASDE (monthly, 12:00 ET since 2013): price effect not significant at 10 min, significant at 30 min; soybean reaction keeps growing from 30 min to the day close
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.window: 2010-2021, 122 WASDE reports, CME nearby corn and K-IXHJ
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.detail: Anderson, McKenzie, Noyes (2024) NCCC-134 conference paper (working paper, not peer-reviewed). Event study: return from release (or from the open when released before the open) to +10 min, +30 min and the day close, regressed on WASDE world-ending-stocks surprise vs Bloomberg analyst survey (SUR). Corn: -0.023 (10 min, n.s.), -0.041** (30 min), -0.044* (day). Soybeans: -0.028 (n.s.), -0.061**, -0.124** (day); 10-min vs day coefficients differ significantly for soybeans only. Absorption: slow for soybeans (drift beyond 30 min, surprise-conditional, in sample); corn mostly done by 30 min. Needs the analyst-survey surprise. Contradicts Lehecka et al. 2014 (about 10 min) and Adjemian-Irwin 2018 (few minutes).
D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: We do not find a significant market reaction within the first ten minutes after the report release time. However, we do find significant and directionally appropriate price reactions after 30 minutes. Furthermore, the price reaction continues to grow for soybeans between 30 minutes and the daily close.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: ensuing real-time trading on USDA crop announcements exhibits noticeable volatility spikes in agricultural futures markets, but that this heightened volatility dissipates within the space of a few trading minutes.

D3_s2_scheduled_releases.quote: releases during trading hours result in a relatively smaller volatility spike which extends for five to six minutes at ... Return correlations provide little evidence to support systematic under- or overreaction in prices regardless of when the report is released

D6_directional_evidence.value: first half-hour return positively predicts last half-hour return: DCE soybean slope 0.073 (R2 1.80%), soybean meal slope 0.052 (R2 0.90%), significant at 5%
D6_directional_evidence.detail: Jin, Kearney, Li, Yang, 'Intraday time-series momentum: Evidence from China', Journal of Futures Markets (2019/2020, peer-reviewed; doi 10.1002/fut.22084); MPRA working paper 97134 (Nov 2019) read in full. Venue: Dalian Commodity Exchange (another venue of the K-IXHJ and K-KQRO underlyings). Horizon: first 30 min -> last 30 min of the day; also rest-of-day. In sample (full-sample regressions); trading-strategy returns GROSS of transaction costs. Sign positive (momentum). Only the second-to-last session also predicts for soybean meal; overnight return has power for soybean meal. Data mostly before 2010-2013.
D6_directional_evidence.quote: We observe that the first 30-minute returns positively predict the last 30-minute returns for all four contracts with a slope of 0.073 for soybean, 0.052 for soybean meal, 0.067 for copper, and 0.103 for steel. All of these are significant at a 5% level. Furthermore, the R2 for these four contracts are 1.80%, 0.90% 1.36% and 3.32%, respectively. ... The returns comparison presented in Table 7 is based on gross returns that do not take transaction costs into account.

No half-life or trading test reported. In sample.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: A high level of cointegration is indeed observed during session 2 trading hours, which fades away during session 1. Another interesting result is the stronger intraday cointegration observed on average on USDA announcement days, although the number of observations available is limited.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush (K-IXHJ vs K-KQRO and K-ODAS): intraday cointegration at 1-minute sampling in the day session
D3_s1_relationships.window: calendar 2015, 243 trading days, CME LOB data
D3_s1_relationships.detail: Type: economic spread. Zhou, Bagnarosa, Gohin, Pennings, Debie (2023) J. Commodity Markets 30, 100314 (peer-reviewed; open-access copy). Day session (08:30-13:20 CT, 'session 2'), 1-minute data, missing-data filtered: cointegrated on 180 of 243 days (Table 2), 229 days at 2-minute sampling (NCCC-134 2022 version); Johansen without filtering only 64-70 days. Overnight 'session 1' (19:00-07:45 CT): 52 days (NCCC version Table 7). Speed of reversion related to volume and liquidity; stronger cointegration on USDA days. Horizon: minute-level, within-day. No half-life or trading test reported. In sample.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: A high level of cointegration is indeed observed during session 2 trading hours, which fades away during session 1. Another interesting result is the stronger intraday cointegration observed on average on USDA announcement days, although the number of observations available is limited.

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean crush: overnight session cointegration on 52 days vs 180 in the day session (1-minute, 2015)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: NCCC-134 2022 conference version of [ref] (working paper). Table 7 'Cointegration Summary of Session 1': K-IXHJ open interest rollover 52 days, 2 months, 1 quarter. Two-minute data: 229 cointegrated days in session 2.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: cointegration is mainly playing during session 2 (market official trading hours) of a trading day and significantly less so during session 1 (electronic trading hours). In addition, prices in session 1 are so greatly affected by market noise that even the combining of both sessions yields no additional information

D3_s1_relationships.value: soybean complex liquidity: persistence and positive cross-market spillovers mainly within 30 s; negative at longer horizons
D3_s1_relationships.window: CME soybean complex LOB (2015 per planner pointer, unverified)
D3_s1_relationships.detail: de Boer, Gardebroek, Pennings, Trujillo-Barrera (2022) J. Futures Markets (peer-reviewed). Liquidity, not returns: not evidence of price mean reversion. Planner pointer (unverified): round-trip liquidity cost 9.2 bp K-IXHJ, 12.5 bp K-ODAS, 13.6 bp K-KQRO. Abstract only.
D3_s1_relationships.quote: Liquidity persistence and positive liquidity spillovers mainly occur within 30 s, whereas spillovers for longer horizons are mostly negative. Findings are important for hedgers that hedge the crush and traders who wish to capitalize on the short-term deviation of price relationships.

D6_directional_evidence.detail: Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (2021) JFE 142(1), peer-reviewed. 21 commodity futures (5 metals, 4 energies, 12 softs incl. grains and livestock). Signal r_ROD = return from previous day's close to 30 min before today's close; target r_LH = last 30 min before the close (horizon 30 min, entry at close-30). Closes are the underlying cash close for equity futures (09:30-16:00 ET for US index futures), volume-spike times for others. In-sample pooled/individual OLS plus a recursive expanding-window out-of-sample R2 (min 500 obs) with a Clark-West test; trading results NOT net of costs. Data: Tick Data LLC one-minute bars. Table 2 Panel C: beta_ROD 1.21*** (t 3.63), R2 0.15%, R2_OOS 0.07%. Table 5 Panel B 2000-2020: beta_ROD 1.04*** (t 2.86), R2 0.12%. Table B3 Panel A groups: Metals beta_ROD 1.19*** (4.50) R2_OOS 0.31%; Energies 2.10** (2.34) R2_OOS 0.20%; Softs 0.65** (2.16) R2_OOS -0.01%. Table 6 Panel C: eta(r_ROD) SR 1.42 (gross).
